evals.name: pass-well-structured-skill
evals.expected_output: PASS verdict — no structural errors, instructions are actionable, output format defined.
assertions: Semantic review covers description, instructions, architecture, and completeness

evals.name: reject-garbage-skill
evals.prompt:
Run /review-skill on this skill:
---
name: My Cool Skill
description: Helps with stuff
---
This skill helps you do things. Make sure to do them well. Ensure quality. Handle errors appropriately.
evals.expected_output: REWRITE verdict — name is invalid, description is vague, instructions are entirely declarative with no procedure.
assertions: lint-definition.py reports at least 1 S-code error (name not kebab-case)
lint-definition.py reports Q04 warning (no actionable steps)
Semantic review identifies instructions as declarative not procedural
Verdict is REWRITE (not NEEDS WORK — too many issues to patch)
Output includes an outline of what a good version would look like

evals.name: needs-work-mediocre-skill
evals.prompt: Run /review-skill on a skill that has valid frontmatter and a decent workflow, but is missing gotchas, has no output template, and the description doesn't include trigger context.
evals.expected_output: NEEDS WORK verdict with a required changes table that /improve can consume.
assertions: Required changes table has columns: #, What, Where, Why, Priority, Type
Table is directly consumable by /improve (same format as retro recommendations)

evals.name: agent-definition-review
evals.expected_output: Review covers agent-specific checks: tools scoping, maxTurns, disallowedTools, identity boundaries, handoff format.
assertions: Review checks for handoff/output format specification
S10 (name vs directory) is not flagged (agents live in flat agents/ dir)
